decisions.reason: As a dismantling joint closely tied to the firm’s pipeline and valve business, it fits existing technical knowledge, customer relationships, and production capabilities, so the firm is well placed to improve and commercialize it further.

A powder-coated public waste bin uses some metalworking and coating skills but is commercially distant from the firm’s core water-infrastructure knowledge base, making learning, sales focus, and further development less efficient than in its established business.

Although this waste-bin line offers several models and could appeal to municipal buyers, it remains outside the firm’s main application domain, so absorptive capacity and strategic fit are only moderate and resources are likely better used in core products.

Outdoor public ashtrays share fabrication know-how with the firm’s operations but are still a peripheral diversification with weaker knowledge overlap and less scope for cumulative learning than pipeline-related products.
